system.name: WLB-LLM
system.one_liner: a workload-balanced 4D parallelism scheme for LLM training that combines data, pipeline, context, and tensor parallelism

content.subject: why packing long/short documents together (PP level) and sharding a packed sequence (CP level) both create uneven GPU workload

content.key_idea: A single long document dominates whichever packed micro-batch and whichever context-parallel chunk it lands in, so both document packing and sequence sharding create workload imbalance, not just one.

summary: WLB-LLM balances workload across a 4D-parallel LLM training job that otherwise suffers from pipeline (PP) and context-parallel (CP) imbalance. This figure's two schematics show where each imbalance comes from. On the left, (1) two data-parallel workers (DP-0, DP-1) pack the same Data Loader's documents into fixed-length micro-batches for pipeline training; DP-0 happens to pack one long document into a Heavy Workload Micro-batch (red) while DP-1 packs several short documents into a Light Workload Micro-batch (green), so identically-shaped PP-0/PP-1 pipelines end up processing very different amounts of work. On the right, (2) a packed sequence of two documents is sharded into equal-length chunks and mapped onto CP-0 and CP-1; because Doc-0's causal attention span happens to fall entirely inside CP-1's assigned chunks, the triangular attention mask shows CP-1 carrying a 'Much Larger Workload' than the other worker despite each chunk having the same token count.
